newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end firm in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end firm in quiet trade.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended steady-to-firm Monday, in very quiet trade ahead of the Christmas and New Year holidays.

"Palladium was sold early but there was very little action in gold and silver and little likely before the year-end, other than some minor position squaring," Pell Brothers floor trader, Don Tierney said.
COMEX February gold ended up 10 cents at $370.60 an ounce, after trading in a $371.0-370.40 range. Estimated total gold futures volume was 15,000 lots.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $368.60/369.10,compared to the London Monday afternoon fix $368.75 and Friday's New York close at $368.30/80.
COMEX March silver closed up 0.5 cent at $4.863, after trading in a $4.875-4.850 range.
Based on the CFTC Commitments of Traders data, issued Friday, "precious metals show hints of turning around, or just not seeing that much more selling," MCM analyst Peter McTeague said.
"Non-commercials are better buyers in recent weeks, covering short positions and are now net long in silver."
Non-commercials or funds remained net short 37,027 lots in gold futures in the week ended December 17, but were net long 6,137 lots in silver futures.
With the Christmas and New Year holidays falling midweek this week and next week, closing NYMEX and COMEX, trade is expected to be very light.
After the gold fix in London Tuesday morning, the next fix will not be until Friday morning.
In the past two weeks, the precious metals complex has been consolidating or recovering partially from the year's lows seen in late November.
NYMEX January platinum closed down 30 cents at $375.00, but January platinum enters its delivery period January 1 and April platinum now has more open interest.
January platinum open interest stood at 9,973 lots at Friday's close, with 14,882 lots of open interest in the April contract.
"With January platinum moving closer to the first delivery date on January 1, prices could move higher as the shorts hurry to buy back their positions," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
NYMEX March palladium ended down $2.35 at $118.50 but on volume of only 912 lots.
